**Create atomic vectors**

```{r}
### These are atomic vectors

# character (chr)
name <- "Leia"
name
is.character(name)
# character (chr)
gender <- "female"
gender
is.character(gender)

# logical (lgl)
force <- TRUE
force
is.logical(force)

# double (dbl)
height <- 1.50
height
is.double(height)
# double (dbl)
height_cm <- 150
height_cm
is.double(height_cm)

# integer (int)
# 150L, L here means integer
height_cm2 <- 150L
height_cm2
is.integer(height_cm2)
```

**To create "larger" vectors we use the combine function c()**

```{r}
name <- c("Leia", "Luke", "Han")
name
typeof(name)
length(name)

gender <- c("female", "male", "male")
gender
typeof(gender)
length(gender)

height <- c(1.50, 1.70, 1.80)
height
typeof(height)
length(height)

force <- c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE)
force
typeof(force)
length(force)
```

Note:

1.  Vectors can have length zero. **NULL** has a length of zero.
2.  Vectors are ordered set of elements.
3.  Atomic: elements of the same type.
4.  Elements can have names.

```{r}
# Assign names
names(height) <- name
height
```

```{r}
# Another way of assigning names
weight_kg <- c("Leia" = 55, "Luke" = 75, "Han" = 85)
weight_kg
# It is the same without the quotation signs
weight_kg2 <- c(Leia = 55, Luke = 75, Han = 85)
weight_kg2
```

Note:

1.  Vectors are atomic structures.
2.  The values in a vector must be **ALL** of the same type. You **CANNOT** have a vector of different data types

Special Values:

1.  NA: not available (logical, int, dbl, chr)
2.  NULL: Does not exist
3.  NaN: not a number
4.  Inf: infinity

```{r}
int <- c(1L, 3L, 5L, NA)
int
sqrt(-4)
log(-2)
5/0
```

**Use "\#" to make comments**

```{r}
# create a vector
c("A", "C", "D") # a vector created
```

**typeof() and mode() functions**

![figure](type_and_mode.JPG)

```{r}
typeof(name)
mode(name)

typeof(height)
mode(height)
```

Note:

1.  types: logical, integer, double, character
2.  mode: integer and double are both called numeric
